blocks.text: ILOILO CITY — Two rare opahs, unusual among fish for their ability to keep their bodies warmer than the surrounding seawater, were caught off Caluya, Antique, on Thursday, Sept. 17. The larger fish weighed about 80 kilos and the other, about 60 kilos. The catch is only the second recorded occurrence of the deep-water fish in Antique, according to licensed fisheries technologist and biodiversity researcher Flord Nicson Calawag. Locally known as “tabas” and also called moonfish, opah are rarely encountered oceanic fish that inhabit open waters and can range into considerable depths.
